findings.title: Equal-priority crypto providers are silently selected
findings.description: Default, Elytron, and FIPS providers all return priority `200`. When multiple full providers are present, selection now depends on service discovery order instead of rejecting the ambiguity. A non-FIPS provider can therefore win over FIPS. Reject ties at the highest priority while allowing the lower-priority authz fallback.

findings.title: Sequence parsing accepts incorrect content lengths
findings.description: The loop accepts a child extending beyond the declared sequence length because a negative remainder simply terminates parsing. For example, `30 05 02 01 01 02 01 02` is accepted as two integers despite declaring only five content bytes. Bound reads to the sequence content and require exact consumption; add malformed-length tests.

findings.title: Tests do not exercise the larger signature curves
findings.description: All three tests use an unconfigured EC generator, so ES384 and ES512 do not explicitly exercise P-384 and P-521. This misses P-521’s long-form DER sequence length. Generate the matching curve for each algorithm and verify the reconstructed DER signature with JCA, rather than relying only on the implementation’s own round-trip.
